content:
There is a "Copy To" function in Thunderbird. You can use it to copy your emails/folders between different accounts.

For example, you can create a backup email account pointing to your HDD using Maildir format. After activating this backup account, you can select your emails/folders and copy them to the backup account. These emails/folders will then be saved to your HDD and can be access via the backup account just like local files.

Lin said
I think your menu is hidden. As I mentioned, press <Alt> or <F10> to reveal it.

Every windows user who is using a profile created in about the last 10 years has had their windows menu bar hidden by default. All the while Linux and Apple OS have it displayed.

I wrote a blog about the topic in 2012 and the idea was all windows versions after XP at that point in time.

I think after a quick Bugzilla search that it landed in V17 in bug 650170 and the default for new profiles was simply changed.

@John, if you right click on any "blank space on the menu bar or tab bar you will be offered a small menu with the menu bar listed. Selecting it gives it a tick and it is permanently visible from that point on.

If you click on a tab instead of a blank space you do not get that menu you get

So make sure to find a blank space
